solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Impeccable fellow criminal

parts.note: criminal behaviour is lawless, outside the law

explanation.surface: A partner in crime is described as impeccable, an ironic compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impeccable has no faults or defects at all, which is the same as being without flaw.

clue.text: Battled for stronghold, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word for stronghold is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: Soldiers battled to capture a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech FORT and the answer sound the same; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Battled means fought, the past tense of the verb to fight.

clue.text: Bar attire set out for judge

indicators.note: set out signals the letters of bar attire being laid out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Lawyers' courtroom clothing is arranged for the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a dispute is to arbitrate it, settling it as an impartial referee.

clue.text: The French male remains in control

parts.note: le is the masculine form of the in French
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's remains are still kept under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male' specifies the masculine article LE rather than LA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is a lead for restraining a dog, so figuratively a means of control.

clue.text: A cider's mixed in cocktail

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters of a cider's being blended up together

parts.note: the letters of a cider's, including the s

explanation.surface: Cider is mixed into a cocktail drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'cider's' counts as a letter here; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Spinners put back on, being very accurate

indicators.note: put back means the word for spinners is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: tops are toys that spin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bowlers who spin are brought back into the attack and bowl with great accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns TOPS into SPOT; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is a British idiom for exactly right or precisely accurate.

clue.text: Reproduce new way to get things done

indicators.note: new means the letters of reproduce are made into a different word

explanation.surface: Copying something in a new manner to get the job done.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established method or way of doing something.

clue.text: Understood one to be in diplomacy

indicators.note: to be in means the letter for one is placed inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is sensitivity and diplomacy in dealing with people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being a diplomat requires an unspoken understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being stated outright.

clue.text: Unfortunately, Don's away at the moment

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of Don's away have been messed up

explanation.surface: Sadly, Don is not here at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present time, these days, currently.

clue.text: Rebukes for violent pub attacks

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters of pub being thrown about into a new order

parts.note: raids are sudden attacks

explanation.surface: A pub is attacked violently and someone gets told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges PUB into UPB, followed by RAIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold or reprimand them, a synonym for rebuking.

clue.text: Doctor takes boat to capital

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a military doctor
a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A medical man takes a boat trip to a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' simply joins the doctor to the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Antelopes — their turning up is celebrated

indicators.note: turning up signals that in this down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sung means praised or celebrated in song

explanation.surface: The arrival of antelope herds is celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' is a link; in a down entry 'turning up' reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest is a large African antelope also known by this shorter name.

clue.text: Signal to driver to stop — it's a hold-up

definitions.meaning: to thumb a lift, signalling a passing motorist to pull over
a snag or delay that holds things up

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker's thumb stops traffic, causing a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitching a lift means signalling cars to stop; a hitch is also a snag causing delay.

clue.text: Called round on one occasion in vain

indicators.note: round means the word for called goes around the other piece

parts.note: cited means summoned or called, as to court
once means on one occasion

explanation.surface: Someone paid a single visit and found it pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' reads as 'to no purpose' but here means proud of oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vain means having an excessive opinion of oneself, the same as being conceited.

clue.text: Tropic disease

definitions.meaning: the Tropic of ... is the northern tropical line of latitude
a malignant growth or tumour is a serious illness of this name

explanation.definitionFit: One of Earth's two tropics is named after the crab constellation; the same word names a malignant illness.

clue.text: Crowds study the route

definitions.note: plural noun meaning gathered throngs, matching the answer used of a crowd

parts.note: to con is to study or examine closely
a course is a route or path taken

explanation.surface: Crowds look carefully at the route they will follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowds' reads as a verb but is a definition; a concourse is a gathering of people, and the word can stand for crowds collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a throng or assembly of people gathered together.

clue.text: How people who snore sleep?

parts.note: sleeping ... normally means deeply, but snorers literally sleep making a noise

explanation.surface: A wry question about the way snorers slumber.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundly ordinarily means deeply and well, but here it is read as with sound, noisily.

clue.text: Amend paper said to go by the board

indicators.note: amend signals that the letters of paper said need altering into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's correction notice that something should be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by the board is an idiom for being abandoned or vanishing completely.

clue.text: A golfer upset about first putt in game

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed letters go around the inserted letter
upset suggests the letters of a golfer being knocked into a new arrangement
this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: A golfer is upset at the first putt in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A GOLFER into LEAFROG, and 'about' places it around P, the 'first' letter of 'putt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Point learnt afresh, always to be remembered

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

indicators.note: afresh signals the letters of learnt being made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lesson learnt again will never be forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always to be remembered' reads as part of a sentence but is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever, so it would be remembered for all time.

clue.text: Part of a carcase the lion chewed up

indicators.note: chewed up signals the letters of lion being mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A lion chewing up a cut of meat from a carcass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link; 'carcase' is the British spelling of carcass.
explanation.definitionFit: The loin is a cut of meat from either side of an animal's backbone.

clue.text: Run in to stop batsman reaching it

indicators.note: in means the letter for run is placed inside the word for stop

parts.note: to cease is to stop
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A cricket tactic: running in to prevent a batsman getting home.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line a batsman must reach to be safe from being run out; the definition is loose, describing where a batsman gets to.
explanation.definitionFit: The crease is the marked line in front of the stumps that a running cricketer must ground his bat behind.

clue.text: Frankness and love seen in a dog

indicators.note: seen in means these pieces appear inside the word for a dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Honesty and affection are found in a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link before the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is openness and honesty in speaking, the same as frankness.

clue.text: Lines up a ship in port

indicators.note: in a down clue up places the lines above the rest

parts.note: odes are poems, lines of verse
SS is steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Poems line up a ship in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' sets ODES above SS and A in this down entry; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major port city on the Black Sea coast of Ukraine.

clue.text: Advertising campaign that should result in more money

definitions.meaning: a marketing push to sell a product

definitions.text: that should result in more money
definitions.meaning: a step up the job ladder normally brings a pay rise

explanation.surface: A marketing drive that ought to boost income.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is both a sales campaign and an advancement in rank that usually raises one's salary.

clue.text: Turn up to upset company dog

indicators.note: to upset means the abbreviation for company is overturned to read the other way

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A firm's dog turns up to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to upset' turns CO into OC, followed by CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen or appear, the same as turning up.

clue.text: Flying heart specialist

parts.note: reads as a travelling cardiologist, but means the winged god of love who targets hearts

explanation.surface: A cardiologist who travels by air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is shown with wings, shooting arrows into hearts to make people fall in love.

clue.text: Motor and railway transport

parts.note: a motor is a car

explanation.surface: Moving goods by road and rail.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry is to transport something from one place to another.

clue.text: It may get broken — put it down!

definitions.meaning: a best performance in sport is often broken
to set down in writing or log something

explanation.surface: A command to write down something that may be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting best is broken when beaten; to note something in writing is to log it.

clue.text: Students staying at school are the ones who get on

definitions.meaning: pupils who live in at a residential school
people who board a ship, train or plane

explanation.surface: Resident pupils are those who succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Residential pupils live in at school; anyone who boards a vehicle also gets on it.

clue.text: Cultural centre?

parts.note: reads as an arts venue, but a place where plants are cultivated, horticulture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultural' is taken as relating to cultivation of plants rather than the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot where flowers and vegetables are cultivated, so a centre of horticulture.

clue.text: Ray eager to resolve doubtful situation

indicators.note: to resolve suggests breaking down and reforming the letters of ray eager

explanation.surface: Ray is keen to clear up an uncertain matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is an idiom for a situation that is ill-defined or ambiguous.
